note.title: Boom News|爆炸頭
note.desc: Boom News (爆炸頭), the independent Hong Kong outlet run by Tang Ho-wing — arrested for "sedition" in October 2026 — preserved here as a browsable web archive of its Facebook presence.

pageProps.body:
Boom News|爆炸頭

Related: 📰 Press Freedom under Siege | Stand News | Apple Daily

Boom News (爆炸頭) is an independent Hong Kong online news outlet run by journalist Tang Ho-wing (鄧浩榮) — a Chinese University computer-science graduate and former student- and online-press reporter who built the "爆炸頭" brand of street reporting and live-streams from around 2020 — with a following of some 200,000, publishing chiefly through Facebook. On 30 September 2026, national-security police arrested Tang (37) and former League of Social Democrats member Lee Ying-chi (李盈姿, 58) for allegedly "spreading false information" with seditious intent under section 24 of the 2024 Safeguarding National Security Ordinance — an offence carrying up to seven years — over coverage of the 31 August commemorations of the 2019 Prince Edward MTR incident; the force confirmed the arrests on 1 October. Tang was released on bail shortly after midnight on 2 October, having been held almost two days; no charge has been laid. He was one of eight people arrested over the 31 August gathering. The Hong Kong Journalists Association's response — "reporting is not sedition" — and the wider pattern are on the Press Freedom under Siege hub.

Update — bank accounts frozen (October 2026). On 7 October, days after his release, Tang said on social media that all of his personal bank accounts had been frozen — with no advance notice and no formal freezing order shown to him. He said he had been left to rely on cash and could not even take up food-delivery work, which requires a bank account, and that he might have to "resort to begging." No bank has been named, no amount disclosed, and the authorities have not confirmed ordering the freeze. The freeze was first reported by the exile outlet Points Media (棱角媒體) and documented by the China Media Project's Lingua Sinica; the Committee to Protect Journalists and Reporters Without Borders have voiced concern. Cutting off a bail-released journalist's everyday banking — before any charge is even laid — extends the case from his reporting to his ability to live. The pattern sits alongside the overseas asset and funding measures on 🌏 Pursued Abroad and the wider record on Press Freedom under Siege.

Because an outlet that lives on a platform can vanish with a single account takedown, this page preserves Boom News's Facebook presence as a self-contained web archive (WACZ) that replays in your browser — the timeline, photos, videos, reels and about pages as captured on 30 September – 1 October 2026.

Browse the archive

Last archived: 1 October 2026 · capture window 30 Sep – 1 Oct 2026

Replays entirely in your browser via ReplayWeb.page; nothing is fetched from Facebook. It streams only the parts of the 2.6 GB archive you view, so give each page a moment. — open full-screen ↗ if the player above stays blank.

Open full-screen or jump to a section (opens in ReplayWeb.page):

  • Timeline
  • Photos
  • Videos
  • Reels
  • About

Download the archive: boomheadhk-public.wacz (~2.6 GB, WACZ — open it in the ReplayWeb.page desktop app or at replayweb.page → Choose File).

About this capture

  • Captured: 30 September – 1 October 2026, via a browser-based crawl packaged as WACZ with the wacz tool.
  • Scope: the public facebook.com/boomheadhk timeline, photos, videos, reels and about pages.
  • Format: WACZ — an open, self-describing web-archive package that replays client-side; integrity is covered by its internal datapackage-digest.json.
  • Privacy: the public copy has been reprocessed to strip all request/response cookies and authorization headers from the underlying WARC records, so no capture-session credentials are exposed.

Sources

  • HKFP: Hong Kong confirms journalist's arrest for alleged 'seditious' acts linked to 2019 Prince Edward MTR commemorations (1 Oct 2026)
  • ABC News: Hong Kong police arrest journalist and activist over alleged 'seditious' acts (1 Oct 2026)
  • HKFP: Independent HK journalist Tang Ho-wing released on bail following sedition arrest (2 Oct 2026)
  • CPJ: Hong Kong journalist Tang Ho-wing arrested in latest sedition case (Sept 2026)
  • Lingua Sinica (China Media Project): Frozen Out — Tang Ho-wing's bank accounts frozen after bail (14 Oct 2026)

noteIndex.title: SHKO(Save Hong Kong Online)
noteIndex.body:
[![Great Extinction](/assets/extinctions.jpeg)](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/) 
> (_Courtesy: [Hong Kong Freepress](https://hongkongfp.com/2021/11/28/explainer-over-50-groups-gone-in-11-months-how-hong-kongs-pro-democracy-forces-crumbled/), 2021_) 

SHKO (Save Hong Kong Online) is a community-driven project dedicated to preserving the rapidly disappearing websites and online resources of Hong Kong’s civil society and independent media since 2019. In response to the sweeping shutdowns caused by political changes in Hong Kong, we aim to safeguard digital heritage before it vanishes. This project is anonymous, open source, and supported by a global network of contributors.

While most sites in our archive were forced offline due to Hong Kong’s political deterioration, it’s important to note that [[RFA Cantonese|sites.rfa_cantonese]] is the only site here closed not because of Hong Kong’s situation, but due to internal political decisions in the United States.

Explore our full list of preserved sites and archives on the [Collections page](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/).

Recent work: documenting the [[Hong Kong Fire 2025|hong-kong-fire-2025]] tragedy at Wang Fuk Court (168 dead, ongoing probes into flammable mesh/foam, bid-rigging, and a judge-led review), including activism, timeline, and investigation subpages; and the [[⚖️ Jimmy Lai case|faces-of-the-crackdown.jimmy-lai]] — Apple Daily founder sentenced to 20 years under the National Security Law (Feb 2026), with coverage of press freedom impact and international response; and [[🎵 Glory to Hong Kong|glory-to-hong-kong]] — the 2019 protest anthem and the 2024 court order that made it the first song banned in Hong Kong since the 1997 handover; and [[📕 Book Censorship under the NSL|book-censorship]] — how Hong Kong criminalised the printed word, from the banned Sheep Village children's-book trilogy (whose speech-therapist authors were jailed for sedition) and purged public libraries to the 2026 bookshop raids; and [[🗽 Statues & Monuments|statues]] — how Hong Kong's public monuments to Tiananmen and the 2019 protests (the Pillar of Shame, the Goddess of Democracy, Lady Liberty) were removed, seized as police evidence, and driven into exile abroad; and [[⚖️ The Hong Kong 47|hong-kong-47]] — the largest National Security Law case, in which 45 pro-democracy figures were jailed for up to 10 years over a 2020 opposition primary election; and [[🕯️ Tiananmen Vigil|tiananmen-vigil]] — the thirty-year Victoria Park candlelight vigil for the 1989 crackdown, the largest June 4th commemoration on Chinese soil, now banned and its organisers jailed; and [[✊ Faces of the Crackdown|faces-of-the-crackdown]] — a human index to the publishers, students, unionists and clergy jailed, exiled or tried under the National Security Law; and [[🎬 Films & Documentaries|films]] — the protest movement on film, a decade of documentaries and features (Ten Years, Revolution of Our Times, the Joshua Wong doc) now largely banned or unshowable in Hong Kong, gathered with their trailers; and [[📰 Press Freedom under Siege|press-freedom]] — how one of Asia's freest presses was dismantled in five years, from the raids that closed Apple Daily and Stand News to the revived sedition law now reaching lone online reporters.

## Goals
- To preserve as much information as possible before its disappearance during Hong Kong's great transition
- To illustrate a viable method that everyone can use to help preserve online heritage with no pains
- To demonstrate global collaborations to save local digital heritages with best practices

## Quick Facts

We are working on over dozens of [[websites or online causes | sites]] in Hong Kong in the past two decades which has been forced to shutdown or at the brink of disappearing. We'd welcome anyone help [[contribute | participation]] to the content and/or [[sponsor | sponsorship]] our program to sustain it together. 

Examples:
- [[sites.appledaily]] (Extincted)
- [[sites.inmediahk]] (In Danger)
